messages:
customer-team: Hey team — starting ~03:20 UTC we saw a big spike in 520s from APAC customers. They report high latency and some 401 auths. Example request id: req_0a1b2c3d, client IP 103.45.67.89. Dashboard shows traffic landing in us-west instead of ap-east. Any ideas?

maya_support: Thanks — can you paste one full request id + the raw auth header (redact token) and a timestamp? Also which resolver/customer ISP?

customer-team: req_0a1b2c3d 2024-05-12T03:21:11Z. Auth header: Authorization: Bearer <redacted>. Client ASN looks like ISP: APAC-ISP (resolver 203.0.113.18).

ajay_eng: Looking at our ingress logs for that req id: upstream edge handled it in us-west-2. Token validated against auth service which returned 401 because the account region mapping expected apac pool. Snippet: 
```
[03:21:11Z] req_0a1b2c3d src=103.45.67.89 edge=us-west-2 auth_status=401 auth_backend=private-apac expected_pool=ap-sg actual_pool=us-west-2
```

sara_netops: Can you run a dig from a client in that ISP (or paste output from the user) to show the A/AAAA we return and EDNS info? Need to check resolver answer and any EDNS-Client-Subnet stamping.

customer-team: Pasting their dig +short and dig +edns: 
```
$ dig +short @203.0.113.18 api.redwood.example.com A
52.23.45.67
$ dig +norec +noedns @203.0.113.18 api.redwood.example.com +trace
; -> returning 52.23.45.67 (us-west pool)
; EDNS client-subnet: omitted by resolver
```

maya_support: That's helpful — the resolver is returning a cached A that points at a US edge IP (52.23.45.67). Our geodb mapping for that IP cohort should route to apac, so this looks like a resolver cohort cache with stale data. Two things to confirm: 1) what TTL did the resolver return, 2) whether our edge-prefetch TTL was shorter than resolver cache so prefetch didn't refresh their cohort.

customer-team: Resolver returned TTL 86400. Our zone TTL is 1200. Customer resolver seems to keep a long cache (ISP-level override).

kyler_sre: That TTL mismatch is the root cause — prefetch updates our authoritative records every 1200s, but some ISP resolvers override or have long-lived caches (86400). That creates cohort misalignment where client resolver keeps an old answer and keeps hitting the wrong pool. When clients hit the US pool we do region-checking in auth which fails (401) for accounts pinned to APAC.

ajay_eng: To repro locally from our side, run: 
```
# emulate that resolver by forcing lookup against 203.0.113.18
dig @203.0.113.18 api.redwood.example.com +short +ttlid
```
We see 52.23.45.67 TTL 86400. Also running traceroute from that IP range shows path to us-west edge.

customer-team: We ran a quick curl to the edge using that resolver and included headers: 
```
curl -H "Host: api.redwood.example.com" --resolve api.redwood.example.com:443:52.23.45.67 -v https://api.redwood.example.com/health
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
X-Edge-Region: us-west-2
X-Auth-Result: 401 (account-region-mismatch)
```

maya_support: Ok — plan: 1) attempt targeted purge of the prefetch cache for the affected cohort, 2) ask ISP to clear their cache (if possible), 3) add a short-term fallback rule to accept tokens from matched accounts at the us pool for a narrow time window while we drain caches, 4) longer-term we'll evaluate TTL and prefetch strategies.

sara_netops: I'm going to kick a cohort purge job for the resolver IP range 203.0.113.0/24. Command: 
```
edgectl dns purge-cohort --cidr 203.0.113.0/24 --zone api.redwood.example.com
```

ops-bot: Command accepted. Job id=98765. Purge started. Rolling across regional prefetch nodes.

kyler_sre: While purge runs, I'll open a short-lived auth fallback: allow-account-region-fallback(req_id_pattern=req_*, allow_from=us-west-2) for 10m and log any hits. We will monitor for increased risk.

ajay_eng: Also creating a short alert to detect resolver TTL overrides. We should flag any answers where returned TTL > zone_ttl * 10 and correlate with region mismatches.

(about 3m later) ops-bot: Job 98765 complete. Purged cohort for 203.0.113.0/24 from prefetch cache across edge nodes.

customer-team: Re-ran their tests. Dig now returns our apac IP: 
```
$ dig +short @203.0.113.18 api.redwood.example.com A
13.250.200.45
```
Curl shows: 
```
X-Edge-Region: ap-sg-1
X-Auth-Result: 200
```
Errors dropped back to normal baseline.

maya_support: Awesome — thanks for validating. We'll keep the fallback in place for 10m and then revoke. I'll follow up with a postmortem note and recommend we: 
- reach out to the ISP to request lowering their override TTL or support EDNS-Client-Subnet,
- add resolver-cohort telemetry to our dashboard,
- consider bumping prefetch frequency for regions where we see frequent ISP overrides,
- consider a more conservative auth-region fallback policy with strict logging.

kyler_sre: Filing a follow-up runbook entry: "dns-cohort-stale->purge-workflow" with exact commands and troubleshooting checklist.

customer-team: Thanks everyone — big improvement. Please share the postmortem when ready.

maya_support: Will do. :thumbsup:
